resolved_findings.problem: A queued tap could survive a timeScale pause, orientation change or OS touch cancellation because clearing input did not reset the weapon clock.
resolved_findings.resolution: CancellationVersion now propagates system cancellation to motor and weapon pose before deltaTime early exits; FireCancelled clears already queued LateUpdate spawns. Ordinary release retains short-tap behavior. Lost contacts also signal cancellation.

syntax.limits: Syntax parsing only; Unity assembly/type compilation was not performed.

cancellation_integration.source: Production WeaponPose.Update, clock, cancellation tracker and pointer state with narrow Unity test doubles

independent_core_invariants.scope: No dual ownership, finite capped axes, no residual released axes; pause/source cancellation versus normal queued tap

checks.execution_order: Input -200, motor -100, weapon pose Update, animated muzzle sampling/projectiles LateUpdate +200
checks.existing_content: Existing scene is opened rather than recreated; environment root and materials are reused; authored colliders prevent intersecting placeholder placement; existing muzzle marker edits survive setup; camera preset migrates once.
checks.projectiles: Owner hierarchy and triggers ignored; spawn/start overlap plus body-to-muzzle and movement sphere sweeps; saturated query buffers stop the shot; bounded shared mesh/material pool.

notes: OS cancellation intentionally clears both controls and requires release; normal right-stick release preserves left movement.
Current locomotion uses one forward Run clip; directional strafe/backpedal animation remains a visual limitation.
The projectile pool assumes this single-scene prototype, not a persistent player spanning scene unloads.

required_manual_checks: Landscape left/right and notch-safe controls on the actual phone
Two fingers moving and firing independently; normal right release leaves movement active
App switching, rotation, timeScale pause and R reset during Raise produce no delayed shot
Tracers emerge from both animated muzzles and stop at a solid wall, including a muzzle beyond a thin wall
Repeated Setup Mobile Prototype creates no duplicate controls, muzzle markers or environment root and preserves edited materials
